title: Mushaf or printed al-Baqarah 2:183-185
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 1: Ta'if, Isra and Mi'raj, and sawm
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y5 lesson 14 (Mushaf or printed al-Baqarah 2:183-185)
intro: Lesson 14: The rules of fasting: intention, what breaks it and who is excused. To understand the main rules of sawm and how Islam makes fasting easy for those who cannot

questions.q: Explain what a traveller does about fasting in Ramadan.
questions.a: They may leave the fast and make up the days later.
questions.model: Allah allows the traveller not to fast (2:184). He counts the days missed. After Ramadan he fasts the same number: this is qada'.

questions.a: Feeding a poor person for each fast someone can never make up

questions.q: Answer three 'Ask the teacher' letters (in the portal response box): 1) I am ill; 2) I forgot and ate; 3) My grandad is too old to fast. Start: 'Dear ..., Islam teaches ...'
questions.a: 1) Rest; make up the fast later. 2) Your fast continues. 3) He gives fidyah: feeds a poor person for each day.
questions.model: Teacher answers letter 1: 'Dear Yusuf, Islam teaches that if you are ill you may leave the fast and make it up when you are well (2:184).'

questions.q: why is there no special sentence for the niyyah?
what does 'Allah intends for you ease' (2:185) teach about Islam?
questions.a: Islam does not ask more than we can bear; it is merciful.

questions.q: Who must make up missed fasts later?
Back to our ponder: why does Allah excuse some people?
questions.a: Allah wants ease for us; they make it up or give fidyah.
